official.deadline_note: Institutional (CEU) financial aid is awarded in the first two admission rounds only: Round 1 closes 15 October 2026 and Round 2 closes 2 February 2027. Rounds 3 (15 April 2027) and 4 (15 July 2027) stay open to self-financing applicants but no longer consider applicants for CEU financial aid.
official.status_note: Admission to CEU master's programmes for 2026/2027 is organised into four rounds; institutional financial aid awards are made in the first two rounds only, and some programmes such as MESPOM, Mundus MAPP and the MA in International Relations New York City track run their own admissions calendars.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The CEU Doctoral Scholarship covers 'the full cost of tuition, complete with a monthly stipend to assist with housing and living costs'. At master's level the Master's Tuition Award 'may cover 50% - up to 80% of the tuition fee' and 'Full Tuition Award is possible only in exceptional cases'.
benefits: CEU Doctoral Scholarship: full cost of tuition plus a monthly stipend to assist with housing and living costs
Doctoral Stipend of 2,002 EUR gross/month, awarded for a period of 48 months in total
Master's Tuition Award, which may cover 50% up to 80% of the tuition fee, with a Full Tuition Award possible only in exceptional cases
Master's Stipend Award of 300 EUR/month up to 750 EUR/month
Bachelor's Partial Tuition Awards of up to 50% of the tuition fee, up to EUR 4,000 per academic year
eligibility: Candidates from any country can apply for CEU financial aid
Financial aid is granted on the basis of academic merit and is available for most programmes, full-time programmes only
Applicants must apply by the appropriate deadline and indicate interest in financial aid in the Funding section of the CEU Application Form
Doctoral candidates who apply by the financial aid deadline are automatically considered for the CEU Doctoral Scholarship
Students receiving CEU financial aid must not be simultaneously enrolled at another higher education institution unless they hold documented leave of absence
requirements: Hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognised institution, or document that you will earn one before enrolment
Have collected at least 180 ECTS for a two-year master's or 240 ECTS for a one-year master's
Tick the Funding section of the application form to be considered for financial aid
Submit all materials through the online application form - nothing sent by post or e-mail is considered
documents: Complete official bachelor's transcript and diploma in English, issued by the university or a registered translator (copies sent by the student are not accepted)
Proof of English proficiency, or an exemption letter confirming the previous degree was taught exclusively in English
Academic writing submission such as a statement of purpose, research proposal or writing sample
Two confidential letters of recommendation submitted by the referees themselves through the online system
EUR 30 non-refundable application fee, payable once per admission cycle regardless of the number of programmes
selection_criteria: Past academic achievement and the strength of recommendations
English language competency, intellectual merit and relevant work experience
Expectations of the programme, future plans and compatibility with the goals of the academic unit
Most departments interview pre-selected candidates before making the final decision
Applicants are expected to prepare all written materials independently, without generative AI tools beyond grammar and spelling checks
coverage: CEU Doctoral Scholarship: full cost of tuition plus a monthly stipend for housing and living costs, awarded for 48 months
Master's Tuition Award: 50% to up to 80% of the tuition fee, full tuition only in exceptional cases
Master's Stipend Award: EUR 300 to EUR 750 per month
Doctoral stipends are paid by the 4th day of each month into a SEPA euro account, and only once the student has arrived in Vienna
PhD stipends are taxable in Austria and recipients must register with and pay contributions to SVS
application_method: Create the online application in the CEU system and complete the Funding section
Choose an admission round, bearing in mind that financial aid is only considered in Rounds 1 and 2
Upload academic records, proof of English, CV and academic writing, and register two referees
Pay the EUR 30 application fee through the payment portal and monitor the Applicant Portal for decisions
official.application_route: One online application per programme with the Funding section completed; you may apply to up to five programmes, each needing its own complete set of documents and references.
official.study_mode: Full-time only - financial aid is available for most of CEU's full-time programmes
official.international_eligibility: Yes - candidates from any country can apply for CEU financial aid
official.research_requirement: Academic writing submissions such as a statement of purpose, research proposal or writing sample are required by each academic master's programme; some Department of Economics programmes additionally require GRE or GMAT scores as an entry condition.
official.duration: Master's programmes of 1 or 2 years; the doctoral stipend is awarded for 48 months in total
official.description: CEU awards financial aid on academic merit across its bachelor, master and doctoral programmes in Vienna. At doctoral level the CEU Doctoral Scholarship covers the full cost of tuition together with a monthly stipend for housing and living costs, while master's support combines a tuition award with a smaller monthly stipend and bachelor support takes the form of partial tuition awards.
official.program_type: University institutional financial aid (tuition awards and stipends) plus donor-funded scholarships
official.english_requirement: TOEFL 88 iBT (or TOEFL 4.5 for tests taken after 21 January 2026), IELTS Academic 6.5, Pearson Test of English 59, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180, Duolingo English Test 120, or Euroexam Academic C1 pass. Exemption applies if your first language is English or you hold a degree taught exclusively in English, and the Admissions Office may still request a test result. Mundus MAPP and MESPOM set different requirements.

applicant_utility.summary: If you want CEU money you must apply in Round 1 or Round 2, because institutional aid stops after the 2 February 2027 deadline and later rounds only admit self-funding students - that single rule kills more applications than academic records do. The award you are competing for depends on level: doctoral candidates are automatically considered for a scholarship that covers full tuition plus EUR 2,002 gross a month for 48 months, while master's applicants are typically looking at 50 to 80 percent of tuition plus EUR 300 to 750 a month, and full tuition at master's level is explicitly exceptional. Build the application around two recommendation letters that referees submit themselves, since a referee who never uploads leaves your file incomplete no matter how strong the rest looks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong applicants to a full-time CEU master's or doctoral programme who can complete a full file - including both referees - by the first or second admission round.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm which of the four admission rounds applies to your citizenship and programme, and whether the programme runs its own calendar
Tick the Funding section of the application form - leaving it blank removes you from aid consideration
Ask your undergraduate institution to send transcripts and diplomas itself, or through a transcript platform, because copies sent by students are rejected
Register both referees and submit the application early enough that their letters arrive within the one-week window
Prepare an English evidence pack: test score or an official letter confirming your degree was taught exclusively in English
Have a SEPA euro account ready, since stipends are paid into one and only after you physically arrive in Vienna
common_rejection_risks: Applying in Round 3 or 4, when financial aid is already closed
Leaving the Funding section of the application form blank
A referee who never submits, or who submits after the one-week window
Uploading transcripts and diplomas yourself instead of having the issuing institution send them
Missing the ECTS floor of 180 for a two-year master's or 240 for a one-year master's
Being simultaneously enrolled elsewhere while receiving CEU aid without documented leave of absence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: At master's level the uncovered share of tuition when the award covers 50 to 80 percent, plus the gap between the EUR 300 to 750 stipend and Vienna living costs; also a EUR 30 application fee, a EUR 500 registration fee (EUR 1,000 to 3,000 for selected MS programmes), the Austrian student union fee, and health and liability insurance.
document_audit: Diploma supplements must be accompanied by the diploma itself, and both need English versions
If your name differs between your academic records and your passport, the name change must be documented and translated
One-year master's applicants with a three-year first degree who have also completed a master's must submit both transcripts
Recent test scores only: TOEFL and IELTS must be no older than two years, Cambridge and PTE within five, Duolingo within one
alerts: Applications cannot be edited after submission apart from contact details, so submit only when the file is final
PhD stipends are taxable self-employed income in Austria and require SVS registration and social security contributions
Late arrival does not generate retroactive stipend payments - the money starts from your arrival date on campus
Expect an interview if you are pre-selected, and write your materials without generative AI beyond light proofreading
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online per programme with the Funding section completed, pay the EUR 30 fee, let the referees upload, then track the decision in the Applicant Portal against the round's notification window.
